summary: Transient routing stickiness after canary autoscaler preemption causes mixed-variant responses
description:
Issue summary:
Customer QuillHealth reported mixed model outputs for a subset of traffic immediately after a scheduled canary weight increase. The canary variant (redwood/4x-large-v2@2026-03-10-canary) was being ramped from 10% to 25% at 09:00 UTC and the cluster autoscaler preempted a warm canary pod around 09:04 UTC. After the preemption, ~0.8% of requests from the customer continued to return responses from the old variant and some requests returned partial/duplicate tokens (appeared like short reconnects).

Impact:
- Customer-facing request consistency issues for ~0.8% of sessions for 14 minutes.
- Increased error rate of malformed streaming fragments for affected sessions.
- Customer reports degraded endpoint determinism for retries.

Environment:
- prod - us-east
- Dedicated tenant: QuillHealth (enterprise)
- Model: redwood/4x-large-v2 (canary variant @sha:abc123)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a staged canary increase for the tenant route from 10% -> 25% in the Console
2) Ensure autoscaler is enabled with preemption window (spot-like eviction configured for some nodes),
3) Trigger steady request load approximating customer's traffic pattern (short chat sessions with streaming enabled),
4) Observe routing behavior and streaming session responses when the autoscaler preempts a canary pod during the ramp
observed_logs_and_traces: edge-proxy logs (09:04:02 UTC): downstream session 12a4b: upstream connection reset while pinned-route handshake in-flight
serving-runtime trace (09:04:03 UTC): session 12a4b assigned to canary-worker-7, then worker evicted; fallback path executed but affinity token not cleared
console-metrics: canary-traffic-drop spike at 09:04 UTC, streaming-fragment-errors +72% for affected cohort
temporary_mitigation: 1) Temporarily rolled back canary weight to 10% at 09:18 UTC (control-plane action by Support)
2) Applied an edge-proxy sticky-cookie reset for QuillHealth cohort at 09:22 UTC to clear stale affinity tokens
3) Instructed customer to avoid application-level retries for 15 minutes post-rollback to reduce duplicate fragments
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Support (Ana Morales): Customer reported inconsistent outputs after canary ramp. Collected request IDs and initial logs. Opened ticket and escalated to SRE.

2026-03-10 09:28 UTC - SRE (Devon Park): Observed autoscaler evicting canary pod at ~09:04. Edge cookie TTL looked out of sync with our affinity lease. Proposing temporary rollback of canary weight and cookie reset.
2026-03-10 09:35 UTC - Customer (QuillHealth ops): Confirmed saw duplicated short streaming responses on ~5 sessions. They have paused client retries. Asked for ETA on fix.
2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Support (Ana Morales): Performed rollback and cookie reset. Monitoring for recurrence.

2026-03-10 09:50 UTC - SRE (Devon Park): Investigating reconciliation between affinity lease store and edge-proxy cookie lifecycle. Hypothesis: preemption removed worker binding but edge cookie remained valid beyond our lease grace window, causing half-open affinity that routed traffic to fallback path mid-stream.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - SRE (Devon Park): Added transient metric probes to track affinity token clear events and worker eviction hooks. Will follow up with data in next comment.
investigation_notes: - Initial hypothesis: autoscaler preemption removed the in-memory binding on canary worker but edge-proxy sticky token outlived lease TTL, leading to routing decisions based on stale token.
- Evidence: timestamp correlation between worker eviction event and subsequent requests still carrying same affinity token (edge cookie present). No new token issuance observed for those sessions.

- Additional finding: our affinity-lease TTL (60s) and edge-cookie TTL (300s) mismatch allows up to 240s of mismatch window in worst cases. In practice we saw ~14 minutes of anomalous routing because client kept reusing cookie and backend reconciliations delayed due to backlog.
- Reproducer: in staging with forced preemption and artificial delay on affinity-store writes, we reproduced mixed-variant responses and streaming fragment duplication.
- Risk analysis: tenants with long-lived client cookies and streaming sessions are most exposed when autoscaler preempts canary pods aggressively during weight shifts.
resolution_notes: - Short-term: rolled canary back to previous weight and cleared edge cookies for the tenant. Issue impact reduced to near-zero after these steps.

- Medium-term action items assigned: (1) align edge-cookie TTL with affinity leaseTTL or implement token-versioning on cookies so edge can detect stale bindings; (2) add worker-eviction hook that broadcasts affinity clear events to edge-proxies; (3) create canary autoscaler preemption policy to avoid evicting warm canary workers during active ramps.
- Tickets created for engineering work: INT-2184 (affinity-lease-cookie-alignment), INT-2185 (worker-eviction-broadcast), and an RFC scheduled with runtime team for safer preemption rules.
- Customer follow-up: QuillHealth notified about rollback and mitigation steps on 2026-03-10 10:20 UTC; CS scheduled a postmortem and a short runway for a reattempted canary with updated protections.
next_steps: 1) SRE to deliver short RFC by 2026-03-18 for cookie/lease alignment
2) Runtime to prototype eviction-broadcast by 2026-03-25 and test in staging with canary ramps
3) Support/CS to coordinate a controlled re-run with QuillHealth once safeguards are in place
4) Update canary rollout docs to include autoscaler preemption guidance
